business_summary.text: Om Power Transmission Limited is a Gujarat-based power transmission EPC company executing HV and EHV transmission lines (11 kV to 400 kV), substations up to 220 kV and underground cabling on a turnkey basis, plus O&M services.

call_points.text: **Margin outlook:** Management expects to maintain EBITDA margin between 12% to 13% and PAT margin of 8% to 9% going forward.
No numeric FY27 revenue, margin or order inflow guidance was given; management cites only "healthy revenue visibility" from the order book.
Gujarat is still 81.68% of the order book; Rajasthan, Punjab and Dadra & Nagar Haveli & Daman and Diu make up the rest.
PAT rose 81% to ₹4,002 lakh with PAT margin at 8.86% versus 7.84% in FY25.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had claimed a deduction of under Section 80JJAA of the Income-tax Act, 1961 for FY 2019-20 (AY 2020-21). Pursuant to the assessment proceedings, the Assessing Officer disallowed the deduction on the ground that the supporting details were not available on record during the assessment proceedings and initiated consequential penalty proceedings. The Company is of the view that the deduction is admissible and that the relevant supporting documents could not be placed on record due to technical constraints relating to the online submission process. The Company has initiated appropriate appellate proceedings and believes that it has a strong case on merits.
tax_litigation.status: The appeal is currently pending before the Income Tax Appellate Authority. Since the proceedings are conducted under the faceless appeal mechanism, the next date of hearing is not available, and therefore we are unable to comment on it.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: For AY 2017-18 (FY 2016-17), pursuant to a survey/spot verification conducted under Section 133(2A) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 for TDS verification at the Company's business premises, certain ledger records relating to transactions with directors were examined by the Income-tax Department. Based on its interpretation of the said transactions, the Department has proposed/disputed the applicability of the deemed dividend provisions under Section 2(22)(e) of the Income-tax Act. The Company believes that the provisions of Section 2(22)(e) are not applicable to the facts of the case and has initiated appropriate legal proceedings to contest the matter.
tax_litigation.status: The appeal is currently pending before the Income Tax Appellate Authority. Since the proceedings are conducted under the faceless appeal mechanism, the next date of hearing is not available, and therefore we are unable to comment on it.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Pursuant to the assessment proceedings for AY 2017-18 (FY 2016-17) relating to the applicability of the deemed dividend provisions under Section 2(22)(e) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, the Income-tax Department initiated and levied consequential penalty based on the additions made in the assessment order. The Company believes that the penalty is not sustainable as it arises from a matter involving interpretation of law and has preferred appropriate appellate proceedings against the order.
tax_litigation.status: The appeal is currently pending before the Income Tax Appellate Authority. Since the proceedings are conducted under the faceless appeal mechanism, the next date of hearing is not available, and therefore we are unable to comment on it.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: For AY 2017-18 (FY 2016-17), the Income-tax Department initiated reassessment proceedings under Section 147 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, pursuant to information available with the Department in relation to certain transactions examined during the course of survey/verification proceedings. Based on the reassessment, certain additions/disallowances were made by the Assessing Officer. The Company believes that the reassessment and the additions made therein are not sustainable in law and on facts and has filed appropriate appellate proceedings against the reassessment order.
tax_litigation.status: The matter is currently pending before the Income Tax Appellate Authority. The notice has been challenged before the Gujarat High Court, which has granted a stay on the proceedings. As per the Court's directions, no final order shall be passed without obtaining prior permission from the Gujarat High Court.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: For FY 2016-17, the VAT assessment pertains to the credit of VAT deducted at source (Works Contract Tax) by customers. During the assessment proceedings, Form 703 evidencing the tax deducted at source was not available for consideration by the assessing authority. Consequently, the assessing authority did not grant the corresponding tax credit and raised a demand comprising tax, applicable interest and penalty. The Company believes that the tax credit is duly admissible upon consideration of the relevant Form 703 and has pursued appropriate legal remedies against the assessment order.
tax_litigation.status: The matter is currently pending before the VAT Appeal Authorities, and the appeal proceedings are in progress.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: For FY 2019-20, the GST Department issued a show cause notice under Section 74 of the CGST/GGST Act in relation to input tax credit claimed on invoices issued by a vendor whose GST registration was subsequently suspended. Pursuant to the adjudication proceedings, a demand order dated 21 April 2025 was passed. The Company believes that the input tax credit has been validly claimed in accordance with the applicable provisions of the GST law and has filed an appeal against the demand order before the appropriate appellate authority within the prescribed statutory time limit.
tax_litigation.status: The matter is currently pending adjudication before the appellate authority.

timeline.summary: On 2026-04-28, CRISIL upgraded Om Power Transmission's long-term rating to CRISIL BBB+/Stable and short-term rating to A2 for ₹200 Cr of facilities.

On 2026-04-30, Om Power Transmission received a Letter of Intent from Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation Limited for a 220kV Jantral AIS Substation turnkey contract worth ₹44.95 Cr including GST, to be executed in 18 months from the LOA.
Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹174.62 Cr, net profit ₹16.65 Cr.
On 2026-05-20, Om Power Transmission's Q4 & FY26 investor presentation reported FY26 revenue of ₹449.16 Cr (+61% YoY), PAT of ₹40.02 Cr (+81%) and an unexecuted order book of ₹621.28 Cr.
Om Power Transmission Limited hosted an earnings conference call on May 20, 2026, at 05:30 PM (IST) to discuss audited Q4-FY26 results, with audio available at the company’s website.
On May 20, 2026, Om Power Transmission reported FY26 standalone revenue of ₹449.16 Cr and PAT of ₹40.02 Cr during its earnings conference call.

On 2026-05-27, Om Power Transmission disclosed an MSME Commissionerate order dated May 16, 2026 disposing its Section 18 complaint against Chromeni Steels for ₹181.17 lakh of delayed payment (₹104.92 lakh principal, ₹76.25 lakh interest), received by post on May 26, 2026.
On 2026-05-30, Om Power Transmission disclosed a tax order from the Deputy Commissioner, State Tax, Ahmedabad for the reversal of ₹11.61 lakh of ITC for FY16.
Om Power Transmission received a ₹101.56 Cr LOA from Uttar Gujarat Vij Company for turnkey underground cabling at Ambaji.
